subject: Service health measurement & temporary SLA carve-outs - procurement questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@procurecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement Q: how you measure availability/latency + exception path

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking our procurement questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our security and SRE procurement reviews — can you confirm the answers below or point us to the evidence you can supply? BrightPath needs these items clarified before we proceed with the contract:  

1) Uptime/availability definition: how is "availability" computed (rolling window, granularity, per-region vs global)? What endpoint(s) are included/excluded (control plane, model inference, streaming)?

2) Latency measurement: do you publish p50/p95/p99 for production traffic? Do you compute percentiles on all traffic or sampled traffic? If sampled, what sampling rate and how do you ensure representativeness for customer workloads (e.g., embeddings vs generation)?

3) Synthetic / canary checks: frequency, locations, and how those results factor into public uptime numbers vs internal alerts.

4) Customer access to metrics: do customers get read-only dashboards (Grafana), raw metric exports, or APIs to pull telemetry? Any role-based scoping (per-tenant vs org-wide)?

5) Alerting and escalation: what are your alert thresholds, paging policies, SRE runbooks for incidents that affect SLOs, and how do customers get notified?

6) Exception / carve-out process: if BrightPath needs a temporary SLA exception (e.g., during a large import or cross-region migration), what is the contractual process and typical lead time to approve?

7) Evidence & retention: for audits, what evidence can you provide (Grafana screenshots, Prometheus exports, raw request logs, signed summaries) and how long do you retain telemetry for procurement/audit purposes?

If you can point us to a short packet or provide the relevant attachments, that would be ideal. We have a procurement review call on Friday and would like to include your responses.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Vendor Risk | BrightPath Analytics

[Attachment: BP-procurement-questions.xlsx]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@procurecorp.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement Q: how you measure availability/latency + exception path

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized our answers below and attached a short evidence packet. If you'd like, we can walk through this in the Friday call and I can share our Grafana dashboards live. 

1) Availability definition:
- Measured as successful inference responses / total valid requests per-region, using a rolling 30-day window by default.
- We treat the inference API (model inference endpoints) as "in-scope"; control plane (auth/console) is tracked separately and included in enterprise SLOs if contractually required.
- We publish region-level availability (us-west, us-east, eu-west) and an aggregated global view.

2) Latency measurement:
- We compute p50/p95/p99 on production traffic with continuous aggregation. For large customers we provide both aggregated percentiles and per-customer percentiles (see attachment: redwood-metrics-access-matrix.csv).
- Sampling: by default we compute on full traffic for generation endpoints up to a configurable retention horizon. For embeddings, where volume can be very high, we use deterministic sampling (1:10 by default) to preserve representativeness; sampling can be adjusted for Dedicated deployments.

3) Synthetic / canary checks:
- We run synthetic probes every 60s from 8 global vantage points. Canary failures contribute to internal incident metrics and trigger paging if they exceed threshold for a 3-minute sliding window; they do not directly reduce the customer-facing availability number unless corroborated by real traffic failures.

4) Customer access to metrics:
- Customers get a read-only Grafana link scoped to their org, plus an export API for aggregated metrics (CSV/JSON). For enterprise contracts we can provide a Grafana org invite and limited Prometheus remote-write access into a proxy. Access is role-based and can be per-tenant.

5) Alerting and escalation:
- Default production alerts: latency p95 > objective for 5m, error-rate > objective for 1m. Escalation: SRE paging -> engineering runbook -> executive notification. Customers are notified via the console subscription (email + webhooks) and we can add customer-side PagerDuty integration for enterprise scopes.

6) Exception / carve-out process:
- We support temporary SLO carve-outs as amendments to SLA (contract addendum) for scheduled events (migrations, data imports). Typical process: request via procurement -> review by SRE + legal -> approval and documented exception window (usually 48–72h lead time for standard requests). Emergency exceptions are handled case-by-case; we keep a record of exceptions and scope them to specific endpoints/regions.

7) Evidence & retention:
- We can provide: Grafana dashboard snapshots, aggregated Prometheus exports (CSV), signed summary reports for a requested window, and request-level sampling logs (redacted to protect other tenants) for audits. Metric retention: standard telemetry retained 13 months; request logs retained 90 days by default (longer retention available on Dedicated/Private plans).

Attachments included: redwood-metrics-access-matrix.csv (matrix of what we expose by plan) and slo-evidence-pack.pdf (sample dashboard screenshots and export snippets).

Next steps: please confirm which endpoints (generation vs embeddings vs streaming) you need per-tenant percentiles for and whether you need raw log exports for the audit. I can have Grace send the procedural template for exception requests.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-metrics-access-matrix.csv, slo-evidence-pack.pdf]

From: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@procurecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement Q: how you measure availability/latency + exception path

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary and the attachments look useful. A couple quick clarifications before the Friday call:  

- For embeddings: can you confirm the default 1:10 sampling is applied across all customers uniformly (deterministic), and whether we can request a temporary full-collection window for a two-week import?
- For exception approvals: is the 48–72h lead time firm for scheduled events, or does that depend on SRE capacity? We may need a guaranteed SLA on approval time for our migration calendar.

If you can add those two clarifications in your call notes, we can include them in procurement.

Best,
Elena

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement Q: how you measure availability/latency + exception path

Hi Elena — quick follow-up from the SRE side to address both points:  

- Embeddings sampling: yes, the 1:10 deterministic sampling is by default uniform across customers to keep percentile calculations stable. For a limited-duration import we can temporarily enable full-collection for your tenant and flag that window in our metrics exports so percentiles can be recalculated for that period. We ask for a 48h notice to schedule the extra ingestion capacity for Hosted customers; Dedicated customers can request immediate changes with an additional configuration step.

- Exception approvals: the 48–72h timeline is our standard target for scheduled, non-emergency exception requests and assumes typical SRE review load. For procurement we can add a clause committing to a 72h review SLA for scheduled exception requests tied to your migration dates (subject to signature and scope limits). Emergency exceptions (unplanned) remain triaged case-by-case.

I'll bring a short slide to Friday's call showing how we'd represent the exception window in the evidence exports.

Regards,
Grace
Head of SRE | Redwood Inference
